title: [finding] `dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test` asserts an empty child stderr too, so it reds under `--use-env-proxy` exactly as #15234 did
body:
Filed unassigned and **ungraded** by an `os-dev` seat while landing #15234 (PR #17764). ⛔ Not graded, not routed, severity not judged. Out of scope for that card and deliberately not fixed there.

## What was measured

#15234 fixed one instance of this: an entry-guard self-test case that asserts a **literally empty** stderr on a spawned child, which goes red the moment `NODE_OPTIONS` carries `--use-env-proxy` — the flag `check-required-contexts.mjs --verify-required-set` prints as its own remedy, citing #9642.

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` carries the same assertion, at the entry-guard battery:

```js
t('imported, this module prints nothing of its own on either stream', (imported.stderr ?? '').trim() === '');
```

Driven directly on that case's own consumer shape — a child importing `dispatch-gates.mjs` with `--self-test --tier packages/spec/src/index.ts` in its argv, flag as the only variable:

```
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096                 -> status 0, stdout CONSUMER-REACHED, stderr.trim()==''  TRUE
NODE_OPTIONS=--use-env-proxy --max-old-space-size=4096 -> status 0, stdout CONSUMER-REACHED, stderr.trim()==''  FALSE
    (node:28829) [UNDICI-EHPA] Warning: EnvHttpProxyAgent is experimental, expect them to change at any time.
    (Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

The two stderr lines are the runtime's, written before any user code runs. The asserted property is about what the **module** prints, so — exactly as in #15234 — the assertion is a true statement about a real property and the red is entirely spurious.

## ⛔ Why it was not fixed in #15234

Two reasons, both deliberate:

- The dispatch brief scoped that card's landing point to the two gates it names. This is a third file.
- ⚠️ `dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test` **exceeds the 10-minute foreground cap** in the agent container. Measured twice: `exit 124` (timeout) at the card's base commit `ec739e671`, before any diff, and `exit 124` again via `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` on the branch. So an edit there could not have been verified in that run, and an unverifiable edit is worse than a filed card.

⇒ The slow self-test is itself part of why this instance is worth its own card: the gate that would catch the regression is the one nobody can run locally.

## Candidate direction (⛔ not a recommendation — severity not judged)

PR #17764 landed a remedy for the sibling instance that is portable here: spawn an identical child that imports **nothing**, with the same argv shape and env, and compare against what that child prints — the runtime's noise floor, measured rather than pattern-matched. ⛔ Note that a filter written to node's warning **shape** does not work: the `(Use \`node --trace-warnings ...\`)` hint line carries no `[CODE] Warning:` and survives such a filter.

⚠️ Whoever takes this should also decide whether the two files should share one helper rather than each growing its own copy.

## Dedup

Targeted search over this repo's issues for this interaction: 8 hits, only #15234 open and it is about `check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`. The `dispatch-gates` hits (#15539, #13536, #10841, #8162, #7440) are closed and unrelated to this assertion. ⇒ No open twin.

## Re-check

```
node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test   # under NODE_OPTIONS=--use-env-proxy
```

⚠️ Budget more than 10 minutes, or drive the entry-guard case's consumer shape directly as above.
